Once she came back, I find out that the veggie burger was not available...it would have been great for her to have told us that in the beginning.

I had to regroup on what to order and got the tapenade and various apps.  All in all...everything was overly salty.  My friends thought the same of their food.  The drink was decent...nothing special.  My friends thought the burger was avgerage as well...

Maybe it was a bad day for them but I wouldnt go back or take my burger loving friends.
===
Review KlfoquzypG2Jug3R9v7dCA: Disclaimer: this three star review is from a vegetarian's perspective.  I understand that this place is in contention for best (real) burger in the city. 

My (carnivorous) friend was looking for someone to join her for lunch at Village Whiskey so I figured I'd give their veggie burger a try.  It was a standard spicy black bean burger...it was good but I won't ever need to go back again.  My friend seemed to enjoy her burger and the duck fat fries.  I didn't try the fries (quack quack) despite how amazing they smelled. 

It was a decent lunch but definitely a place for meat-eaters.
===
Review 7RfR9GR-BKUtkseBKsI1uA: This is my favorite brunch spot in the city. We go back time and time again. I'm vegetarian but don't let that put you off if you're a meat eater... the meat options look even better!

I've never had whiskey there, but a bloody mary on a Sunday goes down a treat, and they have a great selection of local beers, including some of my favorites, and often they have them on tap.

For food we always start with some of their amazing pickles - usually beets, which come paired with grilled bread, olive tapenade and whipped butter. The olive tapenade could do with being finer chopped and better spiced, but hey.

The veggie burgers come in many variants, and it's pretty much build your own burger. I go for the truffled mushrooms and blue cheese, and it comes with guacamole anyhow. The burgers are slightly curried and very tasty indeed. My only criticism is that the burgers can be a bit crumbly and difficult to hold together. They usually need eating with a knife and fork!

The regular fries are fried in duck fat, but you can order veggie fries which are string fries and pretty good. Make sure you ask for burger and fries at the same time or they can come separately.

They probably have other stuff on the menu but who cares when the burgers are this good!

I ordered the veggie burger (black bean & lentil, with guac & pickled red cabbage), plus bleu cheese, and Mike had the burger plus bleu cheese, also. He had a particularly strong adult beverage and I had an orange creme soda that tasted like a creamsicle and/or the creamsicle flavored flouride foam at the dentist, depending on who you talk to. They were tasty although some were chewier than others, maybe a little overcooked, but I'm not complaining since they're an "off-the-menu" item to begin with.

We were sat next to these stuffy old cornflakes who were getting soused on prosecco and the woman ordered the veggie burger, no bun, with sliced avocado instead of guacomole (wtf) and when the husband's burger came he cut it into dainty little wedges and ate it with a fork (wtf).

J.G. obviously knows his stuff.
